items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I was with Carmen Cavallaro for a year, at 18... he carried a quartet. I mean piano, bass, drums and guitar.

ctx.x: Great. In reading your bio it looks like you were influenced by a musical family, not your own?

Right. I grew up in Sacramento, which is not far from here, and there was a family in the neighborhood, the father had done some conducting in Hollywood and so on and so forth, and they’d moved up and they had a couple of brothers and a daughter, a sister. And they were all involved. And we used to have rehearsals and they were — just right down the street. So when I was very small I would sit outside and watch them rehearse. And I went wow, I’ve got to figure this out. This is — I’m talking about preschool, you…

come through there and play. So I heard a lot of live music. And I was inspired by that, to do something. I played the trumpet first. And I switched to drums when I was in high school. And I don’t know, plus public schools in those days, we’re talking the fifties, were — I’m making a living on what I learned in public schools. I mean I didn’t go to college. I mean I started college and it lasted about a month, I couldn’t stand it. I had to go. That’s with the Carmen Cavallaro thing. He had popped up so I grabbed…
